title: Isolated bootstrap & zero-egress upgrade protocol for Private/VPC
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers running Redwood in isolated VPCs or air-gapped sites have requested an upgrade pathway that guarantees zero outbound egress (no external artifact fetches) during operator-controlled upgrade windows, while preserving the ability to rollback and maintain minimal service. This ticket defines the protocol, operational checks, and acceptance criteria for an 'islanded bootstrap + zero-egress upgrade' flow that works across single-site and multi-site private deployments. Scope covers operator bootstrap, staged image availability via mirrors, artifact signing verification, operator-run upgrade orchestration, and post-upgrade verification. Excludes: on-prem hardware provisioning and network-layer vendor-specific firewall configuration guides (those will be referenced as attachments).
requirements: Support an operator-driven upgrade mode where all required artifacts (images, checksums, signatures, package bundles) are pre-staged to customer-controlled mirrors before upgrade window begins
Provide a deterministic manifest format (sha256 checksums, signature metadata) that the operator validates against local mirror copies; manifest must be immutable and timestamped
Introduce a bootstrap mode that can restore control-plane components from local artifacts without contacting Redwood's public endpoints (no DNS/A outbound)
Define a secure signing verification flow using customer KMS or provided signed manifests; verification failures must abort upgrade and surface an operator-visible cause
Allow configurable staged rollouts (per-cluster/per-node) with automatic health gating and observable canary metrics for latency, token throughput, and KV-cache correctness
Provide a fallback/rollback mechanism that can be executed entirely from the operator plane using mirrored artifacts and does not rely on external downloads
Expose preflight checks that validate mirror completeness, bandwidth estimate for staged transfer, disk capacity, and checksum fidelity before allowing zero-egress upgrade to start
Telemetry: during zero-egress flows, only anonymized, opt-in telemetry may be sent; default must be no outbound telemetry unless explicitly enabled by customer
Operator CLI and Console: features to mark a mirror as 'trusted' and to run a dry-run upgrade verification against the mirror (no changes applied)
acceptance_criteria: Given a customer mirror populated with the release bundle, the upgrade runner must be able to complete a full control-plane upgrade without outbound network access; success is signaled by an 'all components restarted and healthy' status
All artifacts applied during the upgrade must match manifest checksums and signatures; any mismatch must halt the upgrade and leave the cluster in the pre-upgrade state
A simulated failure introduced into the canary subset must trigger automatic rollback to pre-upgrade images within the configured SLA (default: 15 minutes for detection + rollback initiation)
Preflight validator returns pass/fail with explicit remediation steps for any failure (e.g., missing image, insufficient disk, checksum mismatch)

No outbound connections to Redwood-hosted endpoints are observed during a zero-egress upgrade when deployment is configured for offline-only mode (verified by network packet capture in acceptance test harness)
Operator-run dry-run produces a human-readable report (console + downloadable JSON) describing exactly which artifacts will be changed and the expected sequence of operations
Security review sign-off captured: manifest format reviewed; signing verification uses customer KMS or equivalent and meets crypto policy; security_review_required = true
End-to-end acceptance test executed in a CI environment that mirrors an air-gapped topology (VMs with blocked egress) and covers upgrade, canary failure, and rollback scenarios
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Specs & Signing: Finalize manifest schema, signing key patterns, and operator verification API (Design + Security + Eng)
Phase 1 - Mirror tooling: Provide scripts and operator docs to create a complete local mirror (images, checksums, signatures). Publish 'mirror completeness' reporter
Phase 2 - Preflight & Dry-run: Implement preflight checks, dry-run output, and operator Console surface for mirror trust
Phase 3 - Offline Upgrade Runner: Implement the offline upgrade flow that sources artifacts only from trusted mirrors, with health gating and rollback hooks
Phase 4 - Test Harness & CI: Build an isolated test harness that can simulate limited-network and fully-blocked egress topologies; run acceptance scenarios
Phase 5 - Documentation & Runbooks: Publish customer-facing runbook, network hardening checklist, and operator troubleshooting guide
Phase 6 - Pilot: Run with 2 customers (one single-site, one multi-site) to validate operational assumptions and telemetry opt-in UX
Phase 7 - GA: Release with private-2025.03 and capture post-release metrics and incident learnings
